faq.q: How does a cactus store water?
faq.a: A cactus stores water in its thick, spongy stem. The stem has folds that open out so it can swell up after rain, then slowly shrink as it uses the water.
asks: Where does a cactus keep water?

faq.a: Spines are very thin leaves. They lose far less water than wide leaves, shade the stem a little, and protect the juicy cactus from animals.
Desert plants store water, lose as little as possible with small leaves or spines and waxy skins, and grow roots that are very wide or very deep.
asks: How do plants live in deserts?

faq.a: Most cactuses have spines instead of normal leaves. Their green stems do the food-making job that leaves do in other plants.
asks: Where does a cactus make food?

faq.q: Why does a cactus open its pores at night?
faq.a: Plants lose water through tiny holes when they take in air. At night it is cooler, so a cactus loses much less water by opening them then.

facts: A large saguaro cactus can take up hundreds of litres of water after a single heavy rain.
Cactus spines are modified leaves; the green stem carries out photosynthesis.
Many cacti open their stomata at night to save water (CAM photosynthesis).

quiz.say: Why does a cactus have spines instead of big flat leaves?
quiz.why: Spines lose far less water than wide leaves and also protect the stem.

wrong.1: Cactuses do not eat insects; spines save water and guard the stem.
wrong.2: Spines do not speed up growth; cactuses grow slowly.
